To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We report on two zirconium-oxo frameworks with the same topology but with different building blocks.
the dimeric Zirconium-oxo cluster [Zr12(OH)8O8] can be isolated from solution and used as a molecular building unit in metal-organic frameworks.
We have developed a novel strategy for synthesizing a Zr-MOF with an intact dimer of Zr12 as molecular building block.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of novel metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and the investigation of their properties.
the synthesis and characterization of new porous metal-organic frameworks with the Zr12 oxocluster as a building unit.
the design of new molecular building blocks and the development of new synthetic strategies for their use in the construction of new materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Zr12 oxocluster is stable in the presence of phosphine based linkers but not in the presence of carboxylate based linkers.
the Zr12 cluster in the UiO-66 family can be preserved by partial substitution of the acetate ligand with a phosphine based ligand.
the dimeric Zirconium cluster can act as a molecular building block in the synthesis of a new Zirconium-organic framework.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can control the incorporation of molecular building blocks in metal organic frameworks.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of incorporating molecular building blocks into metal-organic frameworks.
the Zr12 cluster can be used as molecular building block to construct porous metal-organic framework materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a dimeric Zirconium oxo cluster can be used as molecular building block in a new porous framework.
the dimeric Z12 unit can be incorporated as a molecular building block in a new Zr-MOF.
the dimeric Z12 cluster unit is not a stable building block in the presence of a large excess of phosphine based linker.
